podcast.title: Opening Act for The Beatles (1964)
podcast.body: Jackie De Shannon was one of the opening acts for The Beatles' concert at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto on September 6, 1964. She, along with the other support acts, was booed by the audience who were impatient and only wanted to see The Beatles. "As the opening bands, which included...the Celterie Jackie De Shannon hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Original "Needles and Pins" Structure Flaw
podcast.body: DeShannon's original version of "Needles and Pins" contained only about 90 seconds of actual song, ending with a minute of vamping with placeholder lyrics that didn't work well for her record. "Dishanan's original, was really only about 90 seconds worth of actual song in Needles and pins, and Dishanan's version ends with a minute or so of vamping."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 113: "Needles and Pins" by The Searchers

podcast.title: Songwriter Partnership with Sharon Sheely
podcast.body: Jackie DeShannon formed a writing partnership with Sharon Sheely, who was Eddie Cochran's girlfriend and was with him in the fatal car crash. "A singer-songwriter who had started up a writing partnership with Sharon Sheely, the writer who had been Eddie Cockburn's girlfriend, and in the fatal car crash with him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 113: "Needles and Pins" by The Searchers

podcast.title: Uncredited Authorship of "Needles and Pins"
podcast.body: DeShannon maintains she co-wrote "Needles and Pins" with Sonny Bono and Jack Nitzsche, believing her name was omitted from the credits due to their alleged abusive and misogynistic nature. "Jackie Dishanan insists that she co-wrote the song with them, but her name was left off the credit."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
